queue.title: CI triage -- three hub tests red on Linux, green on this machine?
queue.detail: Done at iteration 2. Verdict: ONE cause, all three tests, and it is a TEST-HARNESS ARTEFACT -- filed F285 (B). The suite runs on sqlite+aiosqlite:///:memory: (hub/tests/conftest.py:19), whose aiosqlite pool is a StaticPool: one DBAPI connection shared by every AsyncSession, so a finishing HTTP request's reset-on-return ROLLBACK erases a background run's in-flight INSERT and record_agent_output's db.refresh(row) raises 'Could not refresh instance'. Measured (memory=StaticPool, file=AsyncAdaptedQueuePool), reduced in scripts/drive/staticpool_shared_connection.py, and reproduced inside the real suite with CI's exact error via scripts/drive/churn_sessions_plugin.py at CHURN_DELAY=0.3. Not reachable in production: config.py:16 is always file-backed. Two further findings: F286 (B) -- a real product gap, _execute_run's exception handler gates the queue redrain (:2358) on already_terminal, so an exception between the terminal commit (:2174) and the normal redrain (:2281) strands queued input with no tick to recover it; F287 (C) -- the refresh is dead weight (expire_on_commit=False, timestamp is a Python-side default) and costs one SELECT per output row.

TESTPLAN.md's T-DEP, T-HOP, T-CONC, T-VOL, T-DRIFT and T-BUDGET are all still unrun and are the natural replacement for 'the next row'.

CI's three failures are ONE cause and it is the test harness, not the product (F285). The suite runs in-memory, whose SQLAlchemy pool is a StaticPool -- every AsyncSession shares one connection, so any request finishing rolls back whatever a background run is writing. Reproduced on this machine with CI's exact error (scripts/drive/churn_sessions_plugin.py, CHURN_DELAY=0.3) and shown not to occur on a file-backed engine, which is the only kind production uses. WHICH FIX is the operator's call: an unshared pool, a file-backed temp database per test, or per-test engine disposal. They differ in how much of the suite has to be re-timed. Until one is chosen the branch cannot satisfy the merge gate's condition 3.

F286 (B) is the part of the CI red that is NOT a harness problem and outlives its fix: _execute_run's exception handler gates the queue redrain on `already_terminal`, so an exception raised after a run reaches a terminal status leaves the input queued behind it undrained, with nothing on a timer to notice. It is a candidate for D-4's spec slot if the drive produces nothing stronger.
